title: Total Lunar Eclipse
description: Total lunar eclipse visible from eastern Asia, Australia, Pacific, and the Americas. Moon takes on a reddish hue during totality.

title: Wolf Moon Supermoon
description: First supermoon of 2026. Moon appears 14% larger and 30% brighter than average full moon when at perigee, closest approach to Earth.

title: Blue Moon (Monthly)
description: Second full moon within the same calendar month. The smaller micromoon of 2026 but still viewable with naked eye during nightfall.

title: Annular Solar Eclipse
description: Annular solar eclipse creates a 'ring of fire' effect. Visible from Antarctica, southern Argentina, southern Chile, and southern Africa.

title: Total Solar Eclipse
description: First total solar eclipse over mainland Europe since 1999. Path crosses Iceland and Spain. Partial eclipse visible in North America and Europe.

title: Perseid Meteor Shower Peak
description: One of the best meteor showers with 50+ meteors per hour at peak. Optimal viewing in 2026 due to new Moon providing dark skies.

title: Partial Lunar Eclipse
description: Partial lunar eclipse with Moon partially entering Earth's shadow. Visible from the Americas, Europe, and Africa.

title: Geminid Meteor Shower Peak
description: One of the best and most reliable meteor showers with 30-50 meteors per hour at peak. Occurs during cold December nights.

title: Milky Way Core Peak Season
duration: Visible May - October, peak July - August
description: New moon conditions provide peak viewing for the Milky Way galactic core. Best viewed from dark sky locations, highest in the southern sky around midnight.

title: Comet Encke Perihelion
description: Periodic comet 2P/Encke reaches perihelion (closest to Sun). May reach magnitude 5-6, visible with binoculars in evening sky from late December to February from both hemispheres.

title: Venus-Mercury Triple Conjunction
description: Rare triple conjunction of Venus and Mercury occurring three times over several months. Bright planetary pair visible to naked eye at dusk.

title: Seasonal Blue Moon
description: Third of four full moons in an astronomical season. A seasonal blue moon, rarer than monthly blue moons, defined by seasonal definitions.

title: Annular Solar Eclipse
description: Annular solar eclipse with 'ring of fire' effect. Visible from southern Chile, Argentina, Atlantic Ocean, and southern Africa.

title: Total Solar Eclipse
duration: 6 minutes 23 seconds of totality (longest of 21st century for land)
description: The longest total solar eclipse visible from land in the 21st century. Path crosses Morocco, Spain, Algeria, Libya, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Yemen, and Somalia.

title: Aurora Borealis Peak Season
duration: Active September - April, peak March & September
description: Solar Cycle 25 near peak brings strong geomagnetic activity. Autumn equinox enhances aurora visibility from Arctic regions (Norway, Iceland, Alaska). Best viewing around local midnight.

title: Partial Lunar Eclipse
description: Partial lunar eclipse with Moon partially entering Earth's shadow. Visible from the Americas, Europe, and Africa.

title: Annular Solar Eclipse
description: Annular solar eclipse with 'ring of fire' effect lasting over 10 minutes. Visible from Ecuador, Peru, Brazil, Suriname, Spain, and Portugal.

title: Total Solar Eclipse
description: Total solar eclipse with path crossing Australia and New Zealand. Visible from Southeast Asia, East Indies, and Australia.

title: Partial Lunar Eclipse
description: Partial lunar eclipse visible from Europe, Africa, Asia, and Australia.

title: Total Lunar Eclipse
description: Special New Year's Eve total lunar eclipse. Moon glows red during totality. Visible from Europe, Africa, Asia, Australia, and Pacific region.

title: Blue Moon (Monthly)
description: Second full moon within December calendar month, coinciding with total lunar eclipse. A rare 'Blood Blue Moon' event on New Year's Eve.

title: Partial Solar Eclipse
description: Partial solar eclipse with Moon covering up to 87% of Sun's disk. Visible from North America and Central America.

title: Total Lunar Eclipse
description: Near-worldwide total lunar eclipse visible from the Americas, Europe, Africa, and Middle East. One of the year's most observed eclipse events.

title: Total Lunar Eclipse
description: Total lunar eclipse visible from the Americas, Europe, Africa, and Asia. Moon takes on striking reddish hue during totality.

title: Annular Solar Eclipse
description: Annular solar eclipse creates 'ring of fire' effect. Visible from southern Europe, central Africa, Turkey, Russia, northern China, and Japan.

title: Partial Lunar Eclipse
description: Partial lunar eclipse with Moon partially entering Earth's shadow. Visible from Europe, Africa, Asia, and Australia.

title: Total Solar Eclipse
description: Total solar eclipse with path crossing Botswana, South Africa, and Australia. Visible from southern Africa, southern Indian Ocean, East Indies, and Australia.
